# Decisions

Rules that span modules, from each package's `Decisions:`. Owner rules end with `(owner)`.

## Owner

- `mailerlm`: A live send is the owner's act, from the review page or `mailerlm send --yes` in the owner's terminal; agents only dry-run and test-send to the owner's own address. (owner)
- `mailerlm`: Campaigns do not track opens or clicks unless the campaign sets the flag; the stats page says opens are unreliable. (owner)
- `mailerlm`: Nothing that identifies the owner enters git: book title, sender domain and address and the postal address, the campaigns and the contacts live in the private database, set in the web app. Keys live in the gitignored `.env`, `config.toml` holds behaviour only, and the repo ships placeholders (`config.example.toml`, `.env.example`). Why: the repo is public. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: A campaign reaches `subscribed` members of its lists who carry every tag it names; a `confirmation` campaign reaches `imported` members instead. Do-not-mail contacts and contacts without an email are always skipped. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: A frame template must contain the place for the letter (`{{ body_html | safe }}` and `{{ body_text }}`); the built-in template can be edited and reset, not deleted. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: Campaigns, templates, settings and uploaded images live in the database, created and edited in the web app; the book title and every other value belong to the campaign (with defaults in Settings for the sender), never to `config.toml`. Why: the owner runs many campaigns and cannot edit a file for each. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: Images ride inside the message as inline (CID) attachments, so no public hosting is needed. Each is resized to email width (about 600 px, with a 2x file), compressed to a size budget and converted to a format every client renders (JPEG for photos, PNG for line art; WebP is converted). (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: Markdown supports images, tables and the standard elements; raw HTML blocks are not rendered. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: The footer carries the postal address and the reply-to-unsubscribe line. Open and click tracking default to off per campaign. (owner)
- `mailerlm.campaigns`: The sum of a campaign's inline images stays within `[caps].max_image_kilobytes_per_campaign` (default 100 KB); a render that cannot meet it fails and names the image. (owner)
- `mailerlm.consent`: Bounces and complaints suppress automatically. (owner)
- `mailerlm.consent`: Confirmation and unsubscribe happen by reply, not by a public link: no public endpoint. Every campaign carries a `List-Unsubscribe: mailto:` header and a "reply UNSUBSCRIBE" line. (owner)
- `mailerlm.consent`: Everyone, including the first imported contacts, confirms by double opt-in before any campaign reaches them. (owner)
- `mailerlm.consent`: Jev (TypeSafe) reads each reply with its thread and picks one option. An unsubscribe is applied at probability 0.80 or higher, a confirmation at 0.95 or higher and only as the answer to our confirmation email; every other option, and anything below the bar, goes to the owner's queue with Jev's suggestion shown. Thresholds are config. (owner)
- `mailerlm.contacts`: A contact is one person with an email, a LinkedIn URL, tags and a membership in any number of lists; the visual list editor edits memberships behind an Edit toggle. (owner)
- `mailerlm.contacts`: A list may override the sender name and address; the default sender comes from config. (owner)
- `mailerlm.contacts`: Imported contacts arrive with membership status `imported`, which no campaign mails. (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: A live send is the owner's act: the Send button on the campaign page, or `mailerlm sends start --fingerprint`. The send repeats the plan and stops when the fingerprint no longer matches, and the repo's permission settings deny agents the real-send verbs. A test send goes only to the reply-to address. (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: Caps stop a send: `caps.max_recipients_per_send` and `caps.max_sends_per_day` raise, never clamp. (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: Delivery status is polled from Resend's API (no webhook receiver, no public endpoint); reading status needs a full-access key, and a bounce or complaint blocks that person (do-not-mail). (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: Every message carries an idempotency key from the send and the address, so a retry or a resumed send never mails a person twice; only a 429 is retried. (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: Resend is the sender, behind the `MailSender` port; SES can be added as a second adapter. Why: the simplest start, one key, an HTTPS call. (owner)
- `mailerlm.delivery`: Tracking is a setting of the sending domain in Resend; the campaign flags are notes. (owner)
- `mailerlm.inbox`: Replies arrive at a plus-address of the owner's Gmail; only mail to that address is queried, and handled message ids are remembered in the store. (owner)
- `mailerlm.inbox`: The classifier's options are `confirm_subscription`, `unsubscribe`, `change_email_address`, `question_or_comment`, `auto_reply`, `other`; its state is the thread, the list and the sender's current status. Requests are cached by payload and never reach the network in tests. (owner)
- `mailerlm.inbox`: mailerlm has its own OAuth client and token with `gmail.readonly`; no other repo's token is reused. (owner)
- `mailerlm.linkedin`: Nothing in this repo touches LinkedIn automatically: no scraping, no browser automation, no API messaging. The owner pastes and sends every message. Why: LinkedIn's terms ban automation and restrict accounts that use it. (owner)
- `mailerlm.linkedin`: Statuses: `interested`, `asked-for-email`, `emailed`, `confirmed`; a contact who gives an address enters the double opt-in flow. (owner)
- `mailerlm.server`: Errors answer `{error: message}`: 400 for a bad request, 404 for a missing thing, and for anything unexpected only the exception's type, never stored text. Enforced by: tests/test_server.py::test_an_unexpected_error_names_only_its_type. (owner)
- `mailerlm.server`: Every POST and PUT passes one write check: header `X-Mailerlm`, Content-Type, Origin (when sent) equal to Host, and a size limit; there is no CORS, no cookie and no token, and OPTIONS is never answered. Enforced by: tests/test_server.py::test_the_write_check_rejects_a_bad_request. (owner)
- `mailerlm.server`: One lock serialises every write, so two taps never interleave. (owner)
- `mailerlm.server`: The JSON body is at most 64 KB. A picture upload is a raw `PUT` of at most 8 MB, the one exception, because a picture does not fit in 64 KB; it passes the same header and Origin checks. (owner)
- `mailerlm.server`: The server binds the loopback address only and answers only Host headers that name this machine (loopback or `*.ts.net`), else 421. Enforced by: tests/test_server.py::test_a_foreign_host_gets_421. (owner)
- `mailerlm.store`: Only `initialize` creates a database; `open_store` on a missing file is an error that names `mailerlm setup`. Why: a silently created empty store hides a wrong workspace pointer. (owner)
